title: Retention and training use: consumer, enterprise, and API

opening.headline: If it is an AI product from the same company, but the data conditions for personal use, business use, and API are different, where and how will our data be handled?
body: Let's say an employee pastes a list of customers into his or her personal account and summarizes it. The same data can be included in enterprise products and APIs created by the same company. However, the three products differ in how long they keep data and how they use it for training.

In this lesson, we start with the idea that retention and learning use are different questions. Next, we compare Anthropic and OpenAI's consumer, enterprise, and API terms and see what retention periods organizations can set for themselves. Lastly, we explain how the same data is handled differently depending on the route, and summarize how to create a condition table for our product.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain retention and learning usage conditions for consumer, enterprise, and APIs
You can distinguish differences in terms and conditions for each product and plan.

screens.title: Same company, different products, different data conditions
screens.lead: Read the situation below and think about how the same material will change depending on which product it is used in.

visual.alt: Illustration showing the customer list splitting into three paths: personal apps, enterprise products, and API.

paragraphs: An employee pasted a list of customers into his personal account and asked for a summary. The same data can be included in enterprise products made by the same company and in APIs called by developers. On the surface, the same model gives the same answer, but the length of time data remains on the server and whether it is used to improve the model varies from product to product.

For this reason, you cannot judge from a single sentence that this company does not use learning. This is because the answer will vary depending on which product, which plan, and which settings are turned on.
In this lesson, you will learn how to find and read product documentation for terms of retention and academic use.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: If data is stored briefly, wouldn't it be used for learning as well? The demonstration confirms that the two questions are independent of each other.

screens.outro: First, let's think about how much we know about the conditions of the products we use.

screens.title: Do we know the preservation conditions of the products we use?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so think of it yourself first.

items.prompt: Can we tell whether the AI product we use is for personal use, business use, or API?
items.answer: Even for services with the same name, the applicable conditions vary depending on the plan of the logged in account. Putting work data into a personal account is the most common starting point for accidents, so check the classification first.

items.prompt: Do you know how long your conversations are stored?
items.answer: Deleting something from the screen is different from deleting it from the server. Anthropic explains that when you delete a conversation, it disappears immediately from your screen, but is deleted from the backend within 30 days.

items.prompt: Have you made sure that the setting that allows conversations to be used for model training is turned on?
items.answer: Consumer products have settings to enable or disable learning. We often write without knowing what the default and current values ​​are, so knowing where the settings are is the first step.

screens.outro: Now let's see how retention and learning use are different questions.

screens.title: Preservation and learning use are different questions
screens.lead: Tap the toggles to alternate between retention and learning usage to see what each asks. It's good to note that the two questions are independent.

states.label: preservation
states.body: Retention asks how long data remains on the server. For example, by default, the Anthropic API automatically deletes input and output from the backend within 30 days of receiving them. However, there are exceptions even when the retention period is short. If flagged by our automated systems as violating our usage policy, we retain input and output for up to 2 years and classification results for up to 7 years. Feedback sent via the thumbs up button or bug report is kept for 5 years. It may also be kept longer if required by law. In summary, the default retention period is a starting point, not an upper limit.

states.label: learning use
states.body: Training usage asks whether the data is used to improve the model. Even if it is preserved, it may not be used for learning, and vice versa. For example, in Claude for Consumers, allowing model refinement settings allows conversations to be used for training. On the other hand, enterprise use and API are not used for learning by default under commercial terms. The answers to both questions are different for each product and plan, so you should not check one and guess the other. For example, it is a wrong inference to see only the phrase that retention is for 30 days and conclude that it is irrelevant to learning after that period, or to conclude that it will be deleted immediately after seeing only the phrase that it will not be used for learning.

screens.outro: Now that we have differentiated the two questions, let’s find the terms and conditions for each product in the documentation and compare them.

screens.title: Read the 3 companies’ preservation and learning conditions by product
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about retention and learning terms and conditions for each product. You can see that the answers are different for each tab even within the same company.

tabs.label: Anthropic Consumer
tabs.body: This applies to Free, Pro, and Max accounts, as well as Claude Code used with these accounts. If you allow model refinement settings, conversations can be used for training and stored in de-identified form for up to 5 years. If you turn the setting off, old and new conversations will not be used for future learning. Incognito chat is not used for learning regardless of settings. Conversations marked for safety review can be used for analysis regardless of settings. So, for consumer accounts, you need to get into the habit of checking the current values ​​on the settings screen yourself.

tabs.label: Anthropic Enterprise/API
tabs.body: We do not train generative models with code and prompts under the Commercial Terms. The only exception is when Customer explicitly provides materials, such as in the Development Partner Program. The API defaults to deleting input and output within 30 days, and follows the terms of any non-retention contract. Enterprise products preserve conversations so they can be continued within the service, for a period determined by the organization.

tabs.label: OpenAI API/Enterprise
tabs.body: Data sent to the API will not be used to train models unless the customer explicitly consents to sharing it. Abuse monitoring logs are retained by default for up to 30 days, and authorized customers can exclude Customer Content from the logs using Zero Data Retention or Modified Abuse Monitoring. The default for corporate products such as ChatGPT Business and Enterprise is no learning, and for some plans, the retention period is set by the customer.

tabs.label: OpenAI Personal
tabs.body: In personal ChatGPT, the Improve the model for everyone setting enables learning. Even if you turn off the setting, saved conversations are not deleted or hidden, and they are not used for learning new conversations. Placing a conversation in the archive does not change whether learning is enabled or disabled. Draft chats are not logged, but may be kept for up to 30 days for security purposes.

screens.outro: We'll also look at retention periods that organizations can set themselves.

screens.title: Organizational data: retention period determined by the organization
screens.lead: The article below summarizes Claude Enterprise's retention period settings. Selecting a highlighted passage will give you tips for reading the setting.

data.text: In Claude Enterprise, With owner privileges, you can set the retention period for conversations and projects by organization. with a minimum period of 30 days. The period is calculated from the last activity timestamp and is The default is indefinite retention., Conversations within a project are subject to the project retention period.. OpenAI states that in products such as ChatGPT Enterprise, Customer directly controls retention period. Anthropic explains that when a user deletes a conversation, the backend deletes it within 30 days.

marks.span: With owner privileges, you can set the retention period for conversations and projects by organization.
marks.note: Primary Owner or Owner role is set in Data and privacy in Organization settings. Regular users cannot change the organization retention period, so you must designate a person in charge.

If not set, data will remain. If you want to reduce the retention period, you need to set it intentionally. If you reduce the period, out-of-scope data is subject to permanent deletion as soon as you save it and cannot be recovered.

marks.span: Conversations within a project are subject to the project retention period.
marks.note: Even if you set a short conversation retention period, conversations within a project may not be deleted. You should also set a retention period for your projects to achieve the intended results.

OpenAI explains that it provides this control in products such as ChatGPT Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu. Check the documentation for the plan you use, as the scope of control varies depending on the product name.

screens.outro: Now that you know how to read conditions, let's look at an explanation of how the same data changes depending on the route.

screens.title: Explanation: When the same material is used for learning according to the plan
screens.lead: Let's break down the situation where the sales team summarizes customer complaint cases into AI by dividing them into three paths. Select the next arrow to proceed.

steps.title: Organize the case
steps.body: The sales team compiles customer complaint cases and summarizes them into AI. Materials may include customer names and inquiries. Since the results vary depending on which path the same file goes into, first divide the possible paths into three.

steps.title: Path 1: Personal Account
steps.body: If model refinement settings allow, conversations can be used for training and stored in de-identified form for up to 5 years. If you use secret chat, it will not be used for learning. Either way, putting work materials into personal accounts is risky because the organization has no control over the retention period.

steps.title: Path 2: Enterprise Account
steps.body: According to commercial terms and conditions, it is basically not used for learning. Conversations are retained within the service and subject to retention periods set by the organization owner. The default is indefinite, so you should be sure that your data will still be there if you don't set it.

steps.title: Path 3: API
steps.body: By default, input and output are deleted within 30 days and are not used for learning. If you have a no-reserve contract, it may be shorter. However, there is an exception that if it is marked as a violation of the usage policy, it can remain for up to 2 years. Since the API is called by the developer, the contract and terms and conditions set the conditions, not the organizational retention period setting screen.

steps.title: Summary of results
steps.body: The path through which the same data goes determines the result. Therefore, it is necessary to set organizational rules as to which paths business data can be stored in, and create a table with the conditions for each path. In these rules, the paths that are allowed, the paths that are prohibited, and the paths that allow data containing personal information are written down.

screens.outro: Let's continue with how to organize the conditions for each route in a table.

screens.title: Explanation: Creating a condition table for our product
screens.lead: This is an example showing how the rows and columns of a condition table are structured. Each row is a product, and the columns are the questions to be answered.

data.notes: The last column of the table must be filled in. Omitting long-term storage in cases marked as safety violations will result in shorter retention periods than they actually are. In each row, we also write down the supporting documents and the date of reading. The order of creating the table is to first list the products that our organization actually uses in rows, fill in the columns from the official documents for each product, and then leave the empty cells as a list of questions. Comparisons can also be made by adding corresponding products from other companies as rows.

screens.outro: Now that we have the condition table, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: Products and Plans Set Data Terms
screens.lead: The contents of this class are organized into four parts.

paragraphs: Retention and learning use are read separately. Even within the same company, terms and conditions for consumer, enterprise, and APIs are different, and organizations can set their own terms, such as retention periods. You should also note that if you don't set it, the default value will be applied. For example, the default for Claude Enterprise is indefinite retention.

Safety violation indications or legal requirements are exceptions to retention defaults. Keeping an exception column in your condition table and writing down the supporting documents and reading dates will help you double-check the conditions. Also, don't just create the table once and then call it a day; read it again regularly.

Before uploading work materials, first check which product and plan this material goes into, the retention period, and learning usage. If the relevant column in the table is empty, fill in that column in the product document before inserting the data.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Conversations deleted from the screen are also deleted from the server after a set period of time.

checks.intro: See for yourself the relationship between retention and learning use. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: Which of the following best describes the use of retention and learning?
options: If the retention period is short, the data is not used for learning.
Retention and learning usage are separate questions and are answered separately for each product and plan.
If the product is from the same company, the conditions for personal use, business use, and API are the same.
If an enterprise product is not used for learning, it will be immediately deleted under any circumstances.
checks.explain: How much retention is left and how much learning is used to improve the model are independent of each other and vary from product to product.

wrong.0: Even if it is preserved, it may not be used for learning, and vice versa, so the two are not connected.
wrong.2: Terms for consumer, enterprise, and APIs are different.
wrong.3: Exceptions, such as safety violation flags, may remain longer.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. The point was made that the two questions should be read separately.
checks.incorrectFeedback: This view assumes that the two questions are connected. Recall that we read retention and learning separately.

checks.intro: Match the results for each route you see in the commentary. For each path on the left, select the appropriate conditions on the right.
checks.q: Match the following paths with data conditions:
right: Commercial terms default to basic learning not used, organizational preservation settings applied
Delete within 30 days, not used for learning
Can be used for learning and stored long-term in non-identifiable form
Exception allowing retention up to a maximum of 2 years beyond the default retention period
checks.explain: The same data may yield different learning and preservation results depending on the path through which it is accessed.
checks.correctFeedback: We connected all the paths accurately. We understood that the paths determined the outcome.
checks.incorrectFeedback: A few connections are out of alignment. First, separate out the routes with default values ​​and the cases that correspond to exceptions.

glossary.def: This is the duration for which input and output data are retained on the server. It may vary depending on the product, plan, and settings.
Whether user data is used for model improvement. For consumer products, it depends on the settings; for enterprise and API services, it is often disabled by default.
Even products from the same company may differ in terms and data processing conditions.
Conversations, projects, and file data owned and managed by the organization through retention policies.

misconceptions.myth: This company does not use it for learning.
misconceptions.fact: Consumer versions are used based on settings, while enterprise and API versions are disabled by default, so they should be evaluated on a product-by-product basis.

misconceptions.myth: If you delete a conversation, it disappears immediately.
misconceptions.fact: On the screen, it disappears immediately, but in the backend, it is deleted after a specified period.

misconceptions.myth: The retention period is the maximum storage period.
misconceptions.fact: Indications of safety violations or legal requirements may cause it to become longer.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: Retention and learning use are read separately.
The product and plan set the terms.
An organization can directly set retention periods and other parameters.
The condition table must always include an exception column.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: If we were to write down the retention period and learning usage conditions for each AI product our organization uses, which column would be empty?
